# captured 2026-09-22
# exe: /home/ubuntu/.local/bin/mirrord
# args: 
Encountered an issue? Have a feature request?
Join our Slack at https://metalbear.com/slack , create a GitHub issue at https://github.com/metalbear-co/mirrord/issues/new/choose, or email as at hi@metalbear.com

Usage: mirrord <COMMAND>

Commands:
  container     Create and run a new container from an image with mirrord loaded (unstable)
  exec          Execute a binary using mirrord: intercept remote traffic, provide access to remote resources (network, files) and environment variables
  dump          Print incoming tcp traffic of specific ports from remote target
  completions   Generate shell completions for the provided shell. Supported shells: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh
  operator      Execute a command related to the mirrord Operator
  port-forward  Forward local ports to hosts available from the cluster or intercept traffic and direct it to local ports (unstable)
  db-branches   Manage database branching
  queues        Browse the status of active queue-splitting sessions [alias: qs]
  teams         Try out mirrord for Teams
  diagnose      Diagnose mirrord setup
  newsletter    Subscribe to the mirrord newsletter
  ci            Execute a command related to mirrord CI
  config        Inspect or change global mirrord configuration at `~/.mirrord/mirrord.json`
  preview       Manage preview environments (requires operator)
  subscribe     Stream operator interception events for a session as JSON (requires operator)
  up            Run mirrord sessions for services defined in `mirrord-up.yaml`
  fix           Fix issues related to mirrord
  tui           Launch the mirrord terminal interface
  ui            Launch the mirrord local UI. Respects the `$BROWSER` env var
  wizard        Launch the config wizard
  chaos         Manage per-session chaos rules for local chaos testing
  session       Manage local mirrord sessions [alias: sessions]
  kill          Kill a local mirrord session
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
